title: Offence of money-laundering
text: Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge or knowingly assists or knowingly is a party or is actually involved in any process or activity connected with the proceeds of crime including its concealment, possession, acquisition or use and projecting or claiming it as untainted property shall be guilty of offence of money-laundering.

title: Reporting entity obligations
text: Every reporting entity shall furnish to the Director FIU-IND information relating to such transactions, whether attempted or executed, the nature and value of which may be prescribed. This includes suspicious transaction reports irrespective of the amount involved.

title: Suspicious transaction definition
text: 'Suspicious transaction' means a transaction, whether or not made in cash, which to a person acting in good faith gives rise to a reasonable ground of suspicion that it may involve proceeds of crime; or appears to be made in circumstances of unusual or unjustified complexity; or appears to have no economic rationale or bona fide purpose.

title: Integrally connected cash transactions
text: Reporting entities shall maintain records of all series of cash transactions integrally connected to each other which have been individually valued below rupees ten lakh where such series of transactions have taken place within a month and the monthly aggregate exceeds rupees ten lakh. Splitting amounts to remain below the threshold is the classic indicator of structuring.

title: STR furnishing timeline
text: The Principal Officer of a reporting entity shall furnish the suspicious transaction report to the Director FIU-IND not later than seven working days on being satisfied that the transaction is suspicious.

title: Ongoing due diligence
text: Regulated entities shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers' business and risk profile and the source of funds. Special attention shall be paid to all complex, unusually large transactions and all unusual patterns which have no apparent economic or visible lawful purpose.

title: Multiple accounts and identity linkage
text: Regulated entities shall apply enhanced monitoring where a single customer identifier such as a PAN is linked to multiple accounts exhibiting coordinated activity, or where accounts of different legal entities are controlled by common directors or beneficial owners, since such linkage may be used to disguise the aggregate scale or origin of funds.

title: Transactions just below reporting thresholds
text: Multiple transactions individually kept marginally below the prescribed reporting threshold, executed within a short period between the same or connected parties, are a primary red flag indicator of structuring designed to avoid the reporting requirement.

title: Funnel accounts and dispersed inflows
text: An account receiving numerous small credits from many unrelated remitters, followed by rapid aggregation or onward transfer, indicates use of the account as a funnel or collection point (smurfing). The dispersion of senders is intended to keep each credit unremarkable in isolation.

title: Circular movement of funds
text: Funds moving through a chain of accounts or entities and returning to the originator, with small attritional differences at each hop and no commensurate trade or service, indicate layering through round-tripping. Common directorship or ownership across the intermediate entities strengthens the inference of a single controlling mind.
